_comment: Registry of converted plugins for shared/scripts/tools/check_plugin_conversion.py (programme Tz, pilot unit P7). Per plugin: 'a_items' are second-pass items that moved into code, so the live prose must no longer carry them (a 'forbidden' regex per file group: 'skill' = SKILL.md, 'prose' = SKILL.md plus references/*.md); 'b_items' are the checks and records that must exist (a 'pattern' found in 'file'); 'seeded' are the L1/L2 tests that catch a regression put in on purpose, and 'sentinel' the test that must run in the plugin's own report. Paths are repo-relative.

a_items.why: mode, banner and setup run inside `release.py prepare`, not as prose commands
gate answers come from `prepare` (`gates`), the prose keeps no per-mode branches for them

a_items.forbidden: docs/migrations|Do you have to do anything
a_items.why: the upgrade-notes check is code (`release_upgrade_notes`); SKILL.md carries only the status it reads (skill scope: release-workflow.md explains the upgrade-notes rule for readers, which is not a mechanic)
`aggregate` owns the flags; the 'never combine' rule is gone by construction
`close-phase` decides; no prose line calls `orchestrator.py update-step` (F7)
the release date and run id are stored once by `prepare`; the model passes and exports neither
the closing summary is printed by `close-phase`, not filled in by the model (skill scope: conventional-commits.md uses the word "categorized" for commit types)
commit and tag are `release.py commit-and-tag`, not git lines in the prose
sync, aggregate and event steps are `release.py` subcommands (skill scope: manifest-sync.md documents the sync script a person may run by hand)
the tag push is `release.py push-tag`, which pushes the one release tag

b_items.why: the upgrade-notes check exists in code
the release date is stored once in a run state
the PreToolUse release guard is registered
the guard reads the record B1 writes
close-phase runs the read-only verify at the end
